thread:
Maya Patel: quick ask: can someone run a Pareto-style sweep (fp16 / int8 / int4 / fp8) on redwood-rlhf-1b with seq=1024, batch=8. Need latency distribution, throughput, ppl, and a small qualitative diff set vs fp16 baseline. Also capture KV cache hit ratio and token-by-token latency percentiles. Ping @Alex Chen @Samir Rao :handshake:

Alex Chen: got it. I can run the perf jobs on dev-gpu-3. Which eval sets? webqa-1k for perf + summarization-200 for quality?

Maya Patel: yes, start webqa-1k then summ-200. keep seeds fixed and include per-example diffs.

Samir Rao: did a quick desktop sweep to sanity check. numbers (seq=1024,batch=8):
```
fp16 baseline: median 56 ms/token, thr 1.05k tok/s, ppl 11.8
int8 (per-tensor): median 84 ms/token, thr 700 tok/s, ppl 12.0 (+1.7%)
int8 (per-channel): median 79 ms/token, thr 660 tok/s, ppl 11.9 (+0.8%)
int4: median 118 ms/token, thr 460 tok/s, ppl 12.6 (+6.8%)
fp8: median 40 ms/token, thr 1.55k tok/s, ppl 12.4 (+5.1%)
```
rough numbers, no KV prewarm. FP8 wins on raw throughput/latency but ppl delta larger than int8-per-channel. int4 perf looks memory-bound and noisy. uploaded a 30-sample diff set.

Olivia Park: can you drop the sample diffs link? i'll run rouge/qa-acc and flag any user-visible regressions.

Samir Rao: uploaded: https://gist.github.com/samir/quant-sweep-samples-1780456789

Alex Chen: profiling notes: fp8 path benefits from fused attention kernels and fewer memcpy spikes. int4 suffers in attention due to small GEMM tiling; we see GPU SM idle periods during KV reads. i'll run nsys for fp8 and int4 to produce timelines.

Maya Patel: pls include the KV cache hit metric (we exposed perf.counter.kv_hit_ratio). also collect p50/p90/p99 token latency.

Alex Chen: nsys command i'm using: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/quant-1780 --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cuda_api \ 
  ./run_bench --model redwood-rlhf-1b --quant {mode} --batch 8 --seq 1024
```
will run fp16,int8-per-channel,int4,fp8. artifacts -> gs://redwood-perf/quant/1780456789/.

bench-bot: Benchmark job queued: bench/1780456789/pareto-sweep (CI id 99211). Results will post in-thread when done. :robot_face:

Samir Rao: webqa-1k finished, summary (fixed-seed):
- fp16: qa-acc 79.2, ppl 11.8, KV hit 0.64
- fp8: qa-acc 76.0 (-3.2), ppl 12.4 (+5.1%), KV hit 0.63
- int8-per-channel: qa-acc 78.4 (-0.8), ppl 11.9 (+0.8%), KV hit 0.64
- int4: qa-acc 73.5 (-5.7), ppl 12.6 (+6.8%), KV hit 0.61
I attached per-example diffs and annotated ~18/200 summarization cases where fp8 produced lower-quality summaries.

Olivia Park: thanks. initial read: int8-per-channel is the best quality/cost tradeoff. fp8 gives big perf gains but quality drop is borderline for customer-facing paths. We should run a larger 5k sample to confirm.

Maya Patel: agree. proposal: expose fp8 as "fast-infer" experimental tier behind a flag, route internal-only traffic for 2 weeks, fallback to int8 when quality metrics cross thresholds. Olivia, can you propose thresholds?

Olivia Park: propose: delta-qa-acc <= 1.5% AND delta-rouge-l <= 2.0 for a prod-safe rollout. for experimental we can allow up to 3.5% qa-acc drop but require daily monitors and automatic rollback.

Alex Chen: uploaded nsys timelines and kernel flame graphs to gs://redwood-perf/quant/1780456789/nsys/. Observations: fp8 kernels have >60% SM utilization and minimal memcpy stalls; int4 shows periodic memcpy spikes at attention launch boundaries and lower occupancy.

Samir Rao: note on quant config: per-channel int8 reduces ppl delta by ~0.8% vs per-tensor at ~5% cost to throughput. int4 per-channel helps a bit but we need new kernel tiling to recover perf. also use the quantized-kernel branch with the memcpy-batch-fix—otherwise int4 perf regresses.

Maya Patel: concrete next steps: 
- Alex: full nsys + traces for the 5k run (fp16, int8-per-channel, fp8). upload timelines and short summary.
- Samir: run webqa-5k + summ-500 (fixed seeds), attach per-example diffs and aggregate metrics.
- Olivia: draft rollout doc with thresholds, canary plan, and failure metrics (auto-fallback triggers).
- Maya: open a staging AB + infra approval ticket and schedule a 48h canary window.

Alex Chen: starting the 5k job now (cost note: needs approval for prod-like infra). command: 
```
./run_bench --model redwood-rlhf-1b --quant fp8 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --eval-set webqa-5k
```
I'll mark artifacts in the job and tag infra team.

bench-bot: Bench results: bench/1780456789/pareto-sweep -> complete. Artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/quant/1780456789/results.tar.gz

Samir Rao: webqa-5k quick summary (full CSV in artifacts):
- fp16: qa-acc 79.1, ppl 11.9
- fp8: qa-acc 76.2 (-2.9), ppl 12.5 (+5.0)
- int8-per-channel: qa-acc 78.6 (-0.5), ppl 11.95 (+0.4)
int8-per-channel holds up; fp8 still shows ~3% qa-acc drop at scale.

Olivia Park: based on 5k, we should not default prod traffic to fp8. Plan: enable fp8 for internal/experimental routes with clear autobackoff rules. I'll prepare the console flag wording and thresholds.

Maya Patel: sounds good. blocker: infra approval for scheduled canary on prod-like hardware due to cost. @infra-team can you advise on approval process?

infra-team: need ticket with estimated GPU hours and list of artifacts to retain. please CC security if KV caching changes surface PII concerns.

Maya Patel: thanks. I'll open the ticket and attach links to perf artifacts. If no objections, i'll create staging AB by EOD Fri. :thumbsup:
